column6: The āyah on the wall lives inside a storm
Sūrah 13 — "The Thunder"
Clouds dragged across the sky
Weather, voltage, noise — air gone metallic
Peace is not the word
The classical lexicons use it for ground
Not something never disturbed
Everything in this study grows out of it
What Allah calls somebody by
Ṭumaʾnīnah inside your ṣalāh
Same question, same answer
Every joint stops before you go on
The objection āyah 27 is answering
A description of who receives guidance
Āyah 28 does not start fresh
What the one who turned back looks like
The passage does not stop at 28
The journey finishes somewhere else
Show me how You give life to the dead
He asked — and he was shown
Angels sent to a badly outnumbered army
Shortened prayer, and the same root
The question is what it comes to rest on
Continuous with 27 — or standing alone
The argument is not settled. The place is.
A second word in this territory — different root
The same verb used for revelation
Dhāl, kāf, rāʾ
Saying a thing out loud
The Qurʾān's name for itself
Turn away, and the life constricts
And it changes the tone of everything
The earth pounded flat
Ṭāʾ, mīm, hamza, nūn — the same root
Not: become settled, then return
A settled heart is not an unfeeling one
Until his eyes go white from it
…and the heart grieves
Instead of being moved
Everything in it is suspended
And leave it
It is still in the glass
Two men in a cave
No weapon, no plan anyone can see
So Allah sent down His sakīnah upon him
You only say it to someone already grieving
What arrived was a floor
Wanting it badly enough is not the method
Thinking harder is more stirring
The training is already built into your day
He was not told to feel more
Sit with them
Spoken inside a sūrah named after thunder
The heavy thing does not have to leave
May Allah make yours one of the settled ones
